Guinea's military-led government has dissolved 40 political parties, including the main opposition groups, through a late-night decree issued on Friday. 
The move strips the parties of their legal status and control of their assets, with authorities claiming they failed to comply with legal requirements such as submitting mandatory financial statements. 
Opposition leaders reject the accusations and warn that Guinea is now effectively a one-party state. President Mamady Doumbouya seized power in a 2021 coup and promised a transition to democracy, but critics say the decree deepens a crackdown on political freedoms ahead of legislative elections expected in May.

Al Jazeera's Haru Mutasa reports.

Rob Geist Pinfold, a lecturer in international security at King's College London, told Al Jazeera that Iran's new supreme leader delivered a defiant but largely unchanged message. 
He dismissed as false Iran's claims of seeking friendly Gulf ties while targeting only US bases, noting every GCC state—including mediators Oman and Qatar—has been attacked.
Pinfold found no evidence for Iran's claim that US bases in the Gulf are being used to strike it, pointing to Gulf states' pre-war demands that Washington not use their facilities. 
He described Iran's strategy as one of "chaos," attacking all Gulf states to pressure Washington into a ceasefire by making the war too costly, even at the expense of burning bridges with regional neighbours.
He noted a disconnect between UAE official Anwar Gargash's suggestion that a "breakthrough is in reach" and Iran's belligerent posture.

description:
On day 13 of the war, Al Jazeera's Tohid Asadi reported from a devastated residential neighbourhood in Tehran, where US and Israeli airstrikes have caused widespread destruction, collapsing apartment blocks and leaving twisted metal, shattered glass and rubble covering the streets. 
Rescue teams and residents are searching through debris for bodies, as heavy equipment clears wreckage. Iran says nearly 19,000 civilian sites have been hit, and the UN Refugee Agency reports about 3.2 million people displaced. 
Officials say at least 1,400 people have been killed so far, with casualties expected to rise as strikes continue across more than 200 cities. 
Asadi witnessed a woman mourning her husband, with more than 20–30 people killed in that single neighbourhood. 
He recalled the Minab elementary school attack, where over 160 girls were killed while in class. Meanwhile, Iran says it is continuing retaliatory strikes on Israeli territory and US bases, with no sign of de-escalation.

description:
Iran and Hezbollah launch coordinated strikes on Israel as settler violence escalates in the occupied West Bank. Tehran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps confirmed the first joint attack since the war began, with missiles fired simultaneously from Iran and Lebanon towards central and northern Israel. Air raid sirens sounded in Jerusalem and Tel Aviv as interceptions were reported across multiple locations. Hezbollah says the strikes are in retaliation for Israel's intensified attacks on Lebanon, whilst the group maintains its military capabilities remain intact. Meanwhile, Israeli settlers torched a mosque near Nablus in the occupied West Bank, with local Palestinians reporting continued attacks that go largely unpunished.

Al Jazeera's Nida Ibrahim reports from near Nablus, the occupied West Bank.

description:
US President Donald Trump has urged oil tankers to pass through the Strait of Hormuz as Iran tightens its chokehold on the crucial maritime route.
Trump promised safe passage for the vessels but did not provide details.
A fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas trade passes through the strait.
Iran says it's ready for a long war of attrition that would "destroy" the world economy. 
But the US president also said the operation against Iran is not over yet.

Al Jazeera’s Rosiland Jordan has more from Washington, DC.
